title.rendered: I Am the Vine, You Are the Branches: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: Jesus does not say try harder to produce fruit. He says remain. The branch does not strain, it stays connected. Fruit is not your achievement. It is the overflow of abiding in the vine.

content.rendered:
The Gospel For Today | Friday, May 8, 2026

📖 Today’s Scripture

“I am the vine; you are the branches. If you remain in me and I in you, you will bear much fruit; apart from me you can do nothing.”
John 15:5 (NIV) | ESV

📝 Today’s Message

Jesus does not say “try harder to produce fruit.” He says remain. The branch does not strain to bear fruit, it stays connected to the vine, and the fruit is the natural result of that connection. Fruit is not your achievement. It is the overflow of abiding.

This completely reframes the Christian life. You are not a performer trying to produce results for God. You are a branch drawing life from a vine. The vine’s life becomes the branch’s fruitfulness. Your job is not production, it is connection. Remaining. Abiding. Staying in intimate union with the One who is the source of all fruitfulness.

“Apart from me you can do nothing” is not a threat, it is a liberation. It releases you from the impossible burden of trying to produce in your own strength what only God can produce through you. When you feel fruitless, the answer is not to try harder. It is to abide more deeply.

John 15:7 adds: if you remain in me and my words remain in you, ask whatever you wish, and it will be done for you. Abiding is not passive, it is the most productive thing you will ever do.

🙏 Prayer

Father, I choose to abide in You today. Not to strive and produce but to remain and receive. You are the vine, I am the branch. Your life flowing through me is the source of everything fruitful in my life. I let go of self-effort and draw from my connection with You. Produce Your fruit through me today. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

🗣️ Declaration

Jesus is the vine and I am the branch. I abide in Him and He abides in me, and the fruit is the natural result of that connection. I do not strive to produce what only He can produce through me. I remain. I draw. I receive. And I bear much fruit, not by my effort but by His life flowing through me.
